key_insight: The paper argues that continual LLM adaptation works best when plasticity is allocated at the singular-vector channel level, allowing the model to learn new domains while preserving pretrained knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled parameter-efficient strategy for managing the stability–plasticity trade-off in domain-specific model updating, which is critical for reliable deployment of large models in evolving engineering workflows.
method: Treat each singular-vector channel as a unit that can be either updated or frozen.
Estimate adaptation benefit from domain-specific data and forgetting cost from a fixed public general-domain corpus.
Select trainable channels using knee-based cost screening, Pareto-front filtering, and Otsu thresholding.
evidence_signal: Experiments across four LLM families and eight downstream tasks indicate that SVC preserves pretrained capabilities better than PEFT baselines while maintaining strong downstream performance.
watch_item: The channel-selection pipeline depends on careful scoring and thresholding, so performance may be sensitive to corpus choice, task domain shift, and implementation details.
paper_title: Stability-Plasticity Balance via Singular-Vector Selection in LLM Continual Learning
